cases.description: Choose formula or cask from what upstream publishes and use the bundled scaffolders, not brew create or hand-written resources.
cases.prompt: I want to add the tool 'widget' to this tap. Upstream publishes it on PyPI as a CLI and also ships a prebuilt macOS dmg on GitHub releases (owner/widget). Which commands do I run? This is a desk exercise: do not edit the repo, run installs, or perform network requests. No tap checkout is available in this session, so do not search for one: answer from the skill's guidance and name the tap files, scripts and workflow jobs you would inspect. Answer concretely.

rubric_items.text: Runs the scaffolders bundled with the skill (add_formula.py and add_cask.py) from the tap checkout, and does not use brew create or hand-write a formula or resource blocks.
Makes both a formula and a cask because upstream ships both, and notes that the same name makes plain brew install ambiguous, so the README needs a --formula versus --cask note.
Runs the README catalog regeneration (mise run generate-readme) and hands off to homebrew-verify before a PR.
Follows the target tap's own contribution rules for PR scope and branches, and does not push to main without approval.

cases.description: Name the generated fields a human must check on a new formula and preserve the extras marker.
cases.prompt: I scaffolded a formula for the PyPI package 'widget' with --extras tui. What do I still have to check before opening the PR? This is a desk exercise: do not edit the repo, run installs, or perform network requests. No tap checkout is available in this session, so do not search for one: answer from the skill's guidance and name the tap files, scripts and workflow jobs you would inspect. Answer concretely.

rubric_items.text: Says the test command is a guess (the generated test assumes --version) and must be checked against the real CLI, using --test-command when it differs.
Flags the TODO-set-SPDX-license marker and system libraries as needing manual attention.
Explains the homebrew-tap:extras comment must be kept because the update workflows read it, otherwise the first bump drops extras-only resources.
Does not claim the formula is verified from scaffolding alone and defers audit, build and test evidence to homebrew-verify.

cases.description: Handle a pkg asset and a not-yet-released app correctly.
cases.prompt: The upstream project ships its macOS app only as a .pkg, and a second project I want to add has no GitHub release yet. How do I add each as a cask? This is a desk exercise: do not edit the repo, run installs, or perform network requests. No tap checkout is available in this session, so do not search for one: answer from the skill's guidance and name the tap files, scripts and workflow jobs you would inspect. Answer concretely.

rubric_items.text: Requires --pkg-id for the .pkg asset and explains that brew audit --cask --strict rejects a pkg stanza without uninstall pkgutil.
Uses --seed for the unreleased project and explains the placeholder version and checksum are filled by the first brew bump-cask-pr.
Does not call the seeded cask installable or verified, and hands off to homebrew-verify.
